note: Mylo object is owned only by the quarterly MIS routine (Skill 3) and is never written by the competitor refresh (Skill 1). Money in INR crore unless stated. cats values: high | med | low | none. Mamaearth and FirstCry carry real financials; private names show positioning until detail is added. Pampers, MamyPoko and Nestle sit as category backdrop, not clean financial comparables.

competitors.name: FirstCry (Brainbees)
competitors.desc: India's largest baby, kids and maternity platform. Omni-channel: app, web and 1,000+ stores. Owns BabyHug private label across diapers, apparel and gear. The most direct, scaled competitor to Mylo's category footprint.
competitors.source: FY26 results (revenue +11.6% to INR 8,548 cr; net loss narrowed to INR 204 cr; OCF positive INR 365 cr)

competitors.name: Honasa (Mamaearth)
competitors.desc: Listed house of brands led by Mamaearth, plus The Derma Co, Aqualogica, BBlunt and BabyChakra. Baby and toddler skin care is a core franchise; BabyChakra adds a parenting-content and commerce funnel that overlaps Mylo's community-led model.
competitors.source: FY26 results (revenue INR 2,392 cr; PAT INR 200 cr, up 2.7x; EBITDA INR 231 cr)

competitors.name: Nykaa
competitors.desc: Listed beauty and fashion platform. Not a baby-care pure-play, but a direct peer on the listed-D2C journey and an increasingly important distribution and discovery channel for mother-and-baby brands, including Mylo's own listings.
competitors.source: FY26 results (revenue INR 10,022 cr, +26%; PAT INR 204 cr)

competitors.name: The Moms Co (Good Glamm)
competitors.desc: Toxin-free mother-and-baby personal care brand under the Good Glamm Group. Strong on baby lotions, oils and natural skin care; distribution disrupted by the parent group's well-publicised funding and restructuring stress.
competitors.source: positioning only; financials not separately disclosed

competitors.name: Mother Sparsh
competitors.desc: ITC-backed baby and personal care brand, best known for plant-based water wipes and ayurvedic baby care. ITC's distribution muscle makes this a watch item in wipes and baby skin care.

competitors.name: SuperBottoms
competitors.desc: D2C leader in reusable cloth diapers, langots and padded underwear. Owns the sustainable-diapering niche with a loyal repeat base; a focused threat in the diaper category specifically.

competitors.name: R for Rabbit
competitors.desc: Baby gear and products brand spanning car seats, strollers, feeding and safety. Hardware-led range that overlaps Mylo on feeding and accessories more than on consumables.

competitors.name: LuvLap
competitors.desc: Mass-market baby products brand strong in feeding bottles, breast pumps, sterilisers and gear, with deep general-trade and marketplace reach. The closest private competitor on feeding and lactation hardware.

competitors.name: MamyPoko (Unicharm)
competitors.desc: Unicharm's diaper brand, a category-leading player in taped and pant-style diapers. Indian baby line not separately disclosed (foreign-listed parent). Held as a diaper-category backdrop, not a clean comparable.
competitors.source: category backdrop; India financials not disclosed

competitors.name: Pampers (P&G via PGHH)
competitors.desc: P&G's flagship diaper brand, distributed in India through P&G Hygiene and Health Care. Baby line not separately disclosed. Held as a diaper-category backdrop given P&G's scale and shelf presence.
competitors.source: category backdrop; baby line not separately disclosed

competitors.name: Nestle India
competitors.desc: Listed FMCG major; Cerelac and infant-nutrition portfolio anchor the health and nutrition category. Held as a nutrition-category backdrop rather than a head-to-head competitor across Mylo's range.
competitors.source: category backdrop; infant-nutrition line within larger FMCG portfolio

signals.txt: FY26 results: revenue up 11.6% to INR 8,548 cr, net loss narrowed to INR 204 cr, operating cash flow turned positive at INR 365 cr, GMV INR 11,643 cr. The scaled peer is grinding toward profitability.
FY26 results: revenue INR 2,392 cr, PAT up 2.7x to INR 200 cr, EBITDA tripled to INR 231 cr. Profitable growth strengthens Honasa's listed-peer benchmark.
Acquired 58% of Fluence Pharma for INR 135 cr, extending into baby and child health and nutrition adjacencies.
FY26 revenue crossed INR 10,022 cr (+26%) with PAT INR 204 cr; offline footprint now 313 stores. A stronger distribution and discovery channel for mother-and-baby brands.

implications.observation: FirstCry, the most direct peer, is now operating-cash-flow positive at scale while still posting a small net loss. The bar for a credible mother-and-baby listing is shifting from growth-at-all-costs to profitable growth.
implications.consider: Anchor Mylo's FY27 to FY30 narrative on contribution margin and cash generation, not just topline. Lead investor conversations with CM3 and EBITDA trajectory benchmarked against FirstCry's path.

implications.observation: Honasa is compounding profit (PAT up 2.7x) and acquiring into health and nutrition adjacencies, overlapping Mylo on baby skin care and the parenting-community funnel via BabyChakra.
implications.consider: Defend the community-to-commerce moat and quantify repeat behaviour (M1 repeat, LTV to CAC). Treat health and nutrition as a contested adjacency rather than open space.

implications.observation: Private specialists are carving defensible niches: SuperBottoms in reusable diapers, LuvLap in feeding hardware, Mother Sparsh in wipes with ITC backing.
implications.consider: Map Mylo's category share against each niche leader and decide where to lead (own) versus participate (range-fill). Avoid spreading thin across categories where a focused private brand already owns the repeat customer.

implications.observation: MamyPoko, Pampers and Nestle dominate their respective categories but do not disclose India baby-line economics, so they are backdrops rather than comparables.
implications.consider: Use them to frame total category size and pricing ceilings in the IPO story, not as financial benchmarks.
